title: Organic Enforcement and Fraud — National Organic Coalition
summary: Organic farm coalition's policy page calling for stronger USDA enforcement against import fraud, dairy pasture and origin-of-livestock loopholes, and uneven poultry outdoor-access rules.

assertions.quote: This has allowed a surge of soybean and corn imports fraudulently labeled as organic.
to ensure that all certified organic dairy farmers were giving their animals meaningful access to pasture
In recent years, NOC has raised concerns that enforcement procedures, particularly those governing organic grain imports, have fallen short.
Imported organic products are required to meet the same standards as domestically produced organic products.

verdicts.note: USDA requires imports to be certified to the NOP standard or an equivalency arrangement, with import certificates since 2024.

Imports may be certified under foreign equivalency arrangements that need only be 'at least equivalent', not identical; OIG found 25 procedural and 9 technical differences in one arrangement and 68 and 28 in another, with no documented resolution of all of them.

Under USDA equivalence agreements (Canada, EU, Japan, Korea, Switzerland) the partners' organic standards are treated as equivalent to USDA's, so some imports meet an equivalent foreign standard rather than the identical USDA rule.
